wrong.title: Subiza is wrong for you if…
wrong.lede: Saying no is cheaper than a disappointed pilot.
wrong.w1: You need us to dial the forwarding code for you. We cannot. That is a SIM talking to a carrier.
wrong.w2: You need WhatsApp live the same day you sign up. Meta's clock is not ours.
wrong.w3: You want outbound calling campaigns or broadcast marketing. We do not build those.
wrong.w4: You want a general-purpose chatbot. The agent answers your business, not the open internet.
wrong.w5: You want a wall of customer logos before you will try the number. The number is the proof.

faq.title: The ones people actually ask.
faq.q1: Will my customers know it's a machine?
faq.a1: Yes — because we tell them. Subiza opens every call by saying it's an assistant, in the caller's own language. That's partly the law arriving across several markets, and partly the point: what frustrates a customer is not knowing they're talking to software, it's ringing out to nobody. You can hear the exact wording on the demo number above.
faq.q2: What if it says something wrong?
faq.a2: Subiza only answers from what you gave it. When the question falls outside that, it doesn't improvise — it says it can't confirm and fetches you. You also get a list of every question it couldn't answer, so the gaps become things you fix rather than things you find out about from an angry customer.
faq.a3: No. Nothing about your number changes — no porting, no new SIM, no new handset. You're switching on call forwarding, which is a setting on your line, and you switch it off again by dialling ##61#. We show you that code at the same moment we show you the one that turns it on.
faq.q4: What if my credit runs out?
faq.a4: Your phone rings, exactly as it did before Subiza existed. That's the foundational promise of the whole product, and it holds for every failure — out of credit, our servers down, a bad night on the network. Subiza must never make a business less reachable than it was before. We warn you at twenty percent and again at five, and we extend your grace period automatically if the fault was ours.
faq.q5: Where does my customers' data go?
faq.a5: We intend to keep personal data in Rwanda, as Article 50 of Law 058/2021 requires. That architecture is still going through counsel — the privacy notice is the live wording. Recordings are off by default. Your customers can ask us what we hold and we answer within the statutory window. The full privacy notice spells out every one of those routes.
faq.a6: One code, instantly, without asking us. There's no contract to exit, no payment card to cancel, no monthly subscription that quietly renews — credit is prepaid, like airtime, and unused credit doesn't disappear.
faq.q7: Will this work on my phone and my network?
faq.a7: Call forwarding is a standard GSM feature that has existed since {year}. We are still confirming how it behaves on MTN and Airtel Rwanda, including whether the original caller ID survives and what the forwarded leg costs. Until that test is written down, we will not say it simply works. It needs no internet on your side: the call is answered on our servers, not on your device.

how.title: No magic. A phone code that has existed since {year}.
how.lede: This page explains the whole mechanism, including the parts that are inconvenient for us. You should know exactly what you're switching on before you switch it on.
how.s1: You choose when Subiza picks up
how.s1b: Two options, and we recommend the first. Only when you don't answer — your phone rings for twenty seconds first, and Subiza picks up only if you don't, or if you're already on another call. Or every call, if you'd rather never be interrupted and be fetched only when a customer needs a decision.
how.s2: You dial a code on the phone holding the SIM
how.s2b: We show it, we let you copy it, and we open your dialler for you. What we cannot do is dial it for you. A forwarding code is a command from your SIM to your carrier — it cannot be sent from a website, and it cannot be sent by us.
how.s3: We call your number to check it actually worked
how.s3b: We don't trust that it worked — we test it. And we re-test it every week, because forwarding can be silently cleared by a carrier reset, a SIM swap or a handset change.
how.s4: You tell it about your business
how.s4b: Hours, location, prices, languages, the voice it uses, and the limits. Those rules are absolute; the agent does not weigh them against being helpful.
how.s5: It answers, and hands you the ones that need you
how.s5b: When a customer needs a person, Subiza calls you — a ringing phone, not a notification. No answer in twenty seconds, it messages you on WhatsApp with the caller's number in the text.
how.breakLede: We degrade in steps rather than dying. At the bottom of every step is the same floor.
how.promise: The one promise above all others
how.promiseBody: Subiza must never make your business less reachable than it was before Subiza. Every other decision in the product gives way to that one.
how.heading: Dial this
how.plat: Android can open the dialler; it never dials by itself. On iPhone, copy and paste — tap-to-dial links quietly fail there.

pricing.title: Prepaid, in francs, by mobile money.
pricing.lede: The way you already buy airtime. No payment card, no contract, no monthly charge that renews while you're not looking, and no invoice that arrives larger than you expected.
pricing.bannerTitle: Read this first: these are pilot prices
pricing.bannerBody: We do not yet know how many minutes a real Rwandan business consumes in a month — it is the single most important number in our economics and we're still measuring it. The prices below are real and honoured for every pilot business through this year, but the bundles may be recalibrated before general launch. If they change, every existing customer gets at least one month's notice and keeps their unused credit.
pricing.homeBannerTitle: These are pilot prices, and they may move
pricing.homeBannerBody: We are still measuring how many minutes a real business consumes in a month. Publishing a price we can't sustain would be a worse mistake than publishing a range.
pricing.b2c: A voice you record, with consent you can revoke
pricing.b3c: Talk to us about volume. No developer platform.
pricing.momoBody: You approve the payment on your own handset. We can never pull money from your wallet — every top-up needs your PIN, on your phone, that time.
pricing.billBody: Credit is prepaid, so there is no bill to be surprised by. We warn you twice as it runs down, and you set your own hard ceiling.
pricing.zero: Out of credit? Your phone rings.
pricing.zeroBody: Your business never goes silent. At zero balance Subiza simply declines, and your carrier does what it did before — your phone rings.
pricing.freeTitle: What we deliberately don't charge for
pricing.peopleWhy: A three-person business does not have seats.
pricing.setupWhy: It's one code. Charging for it would be charging for our own onboarding.
pricing.offWhy: Dial ##61#. No notice period, no exit call.
pricing.creditWhy: It's your money. Expiry is a penalty dressed as a policy.
pricing.exportWhy: Your conversations are yours, as CSV, whenever you ask.

security.title: Where the data lives, and who can see it.
security.lede: A public page, because Law 058/2021 is not a footer link.
security.residencyBody: We intend to store personal data in Rwanda, as Article 50 of Law N° 058/2021 requires. Phase 1 still uses some foreign managed APIs, and counsel has not yet signed the strong version of this sentence. Until that position is written down, treat residency as a commitment we are building toward, not as a completed fact.
security.ncsaBody: Registration number published here once it exists. Pending is left visible on purpose.
security.access: Who at Subiza can see a conversation
security.accessBody: Break-glass only, alerted, and reviewed. Day-to-day staff cannot browse a tenant's calls.
security.retentionBody: Transcripts default to a year, shortenable by you. Recordings are off unless you switch them on, then they default to ninety days.
security.subBody: Named on this page as they are contracted. None are hidden behind a “and others” clause.
security.breachBody: We notify the supervisory authority and affected people in the window the law sets. We do not wait for a press cycle.
security.hostBody: If foreign inference cannot be authorised, self-hosting moves from a later optimisation to a near-term requirement. That decision is documented in the open questions, not buried.

about.title: Subiza means “answer”.
about.lede: It's the Kinyarwanda imperative of gusubiza — to answer, to reply. The related noun, igisubizo, means both an answer and a solution, which is a coincidence we didn't deserve but will happily take.
about.notice1: Small businesses here don't lose customers because their work is bad. They lose them because nobody picked up. A call rings out at seven in the evening. A WhatsApp message sits unread until Monday.
about.notice2: Rwanda has {enterprises} enterprises. Four in five of them have between one and three people. When that person steps out to the market, the entire business goes quiet.
about.b1b: Most voice AI is built in English and localised afterwards. We started at the other end, on narrowband telephone audio, in the noise of a real shop.
about.b2b: A confident wrong answer damages your business; an admitted gap only frustrates a caller for a moment.
about.b3b: Whatever fails — our servers, your credit, the network — calls fall through to your own phone exactly as they did before.
about.b4b: Meta's verification takes several working days. We cannot dial your forwarding code for you. Our prices aren't final. All three of those are on this website in plain type.
about.whereBody: We're in pilot in Kigali. We don't have thousands of customers or a wall of enterprise logos, and we're not going to borrow either. The only thing we can genuinely show you is the agent itself.
about.teamBody: Founded in Kigali. Names, faces and backgrounds go here before general launch — placeholder deliberately left visible rather than filled with stock photography.
about.address: Kigali, Rwanda. Full street address published before general launch.
about.name: On the name
about.nameBody: We considered other words. Subiza won because it describes the entire product in one word, in the language of the first market.

legal.title: What we do with data, in words you can actually read.
legal.lede: The full documents are linked here. This summary is the version that matters — if it ever contradicts the long form, that's our mistake to fix.
legal.phoneWhy: It is your account and your billing identity
legal.transcriptsWhy: So you can see what was said
legal.recWhy: Off by default. Only if you switch them on
legal.callersWhy: So you can call them back
legal.voice: Your voice recording, if you ask for one
legal.voiceWhy: Never used for any other business, ever
legal.livesBody: We intend to store personal data in Rwanda, as Article 50 of Law N° 058/2021 requires. If any processing step needs to happen outside the country, it requires prior authorisation, and we tell you before it starts. The strong wording waits on counsel.
legal.rights: Your rights, and how to use them
legal.access: Access — write to us and we send you everything we hold, within thirty days
legal.correction: Correction — an error is corrected within thirty days
legal.deletion: Deletion — delete one conversation, or your whole account
legal.port: Portability — your conversations as CSV, free, whenever
legal.appeal: Appeal — if our answer doesn't satisfy you, you can take it to the supervisory authority
legal.n1: We do not sell your customers' data. Not to anyone, not ever
legal.n2: We do not market to people who called your business
legal.n3: We do not train general models on your conversations unless you separately opt in — and that switch is off
legal.n4: We never ask for a payment card, which means there is nothing to leak
legal.aiBody: Every conversation opens by stating that the caller is speaking to an assistant, in their own language, before anything else is said. This cannot be switched off — not by us, and not by the business paying for it.
legal.aiNote: It is becoming law in several markets. It is also simply the right way to answer someone's phone.
legal.dpoBody: Law 058/2021 requires this contact to be published, not merely filed. Here it is.
legal.a11yBody: This website is built for WCAG 2.2 AA. Theme and motion can be changed in the header. If something is unusable, write to muraho@subiza.rw — we treat that as a defect.

auth.asideWhyTitle: Why a number, and not an email
auth.asideWhy1: It's the identity your customers already use.
auth.asideWhy2: It's what mobile money bills against, so no card is ever needed.
auth.asideWhy3: There is no password to forget, and none to be stolen.
auth.asideTwoMinBody: Five short questions. Every one of them is asked because the product genuinely cannot work without the answer.
auth.asideCodeTitle: Why the code sometimes takes a moment
auth.asideCodeBody: SMS travels the carrier network, where a message can be delayed or silently dropped. WhatsApp and a voice call sit under the field as equal routes.
auth.asideCaptchaBody: Bot defence happens behind the screen — a send-versus-verify ratio, one code per number per 30 seconds, and Rwandan numbers only.
auth.asideHear: This is what your callers will hear
auth.asideHearEn: Hello. I'm the assistant. How can I help?
auth.asideLangTitle: Why language comes before the terms
auth.asideLangBody: Law 058/2021 requires consent to be informed. Agreeing to something in a language you read less comfortably is not informed consent.
auth.asideRwBody: Not a fallback. It is the language the agent was built in, and the one it answers in unless you say otherwise.
auth.asideTwoTitle: Why two checkboxes and not one
auth.asideTwoBody: Bundling separate purposes into one tick makes the consent invalid. The contract makes the account exist; marketing is a choice you are free to decline.
auth.asideNextBody: Your phone is about to ring. You hear your own agent before any customer does.
auth.asideRecTitle: The hardest problem in this product
auth.asideRecBody: The number is the account, so there's no email and no password to fall back on. Time is the control. Evidence is only the trigger.
auth.asideNeverBody: Nobody from Subiza will ever call you and ask for a code. If someone does, they are not us.
